data.gender_notes: Lingam is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: In Hinduism, Lingam refers to the phallic symbol representing Lord Shiva. It is believed that the Lingam embodies the cosmic energy and represents the creator, sustainer, and destroyer of the universe. The name Lingam carries the meaning “Symbol of Shiva” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Lingam usually hope their child will grow to embody symbol of shiva and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: A symbol of Shiva's divine masculinity and cosmic energy.

data.cultural_impact: The Lingam is an essential symbol in Hindu temples, symbolizing the divine Shiva. The shape and design of the Lingam can vary widely, reflecting regional differences and variations. Annually, millions of devotees visit these temples for puja, or prayer offerings, and rituals. The practice of Shiva Lingam worship is deeply rooted in Indian culture, transcending social boundaries and uniting diverse communities.
data.spiritual_significance: In spiritual terms, the Lingam embodies the divine masculine aspect of God, Shiva. It symbolizes creation, power, and sexual energy (Kundalini). Hindus believe that Shiva's energy is present in all male deities. The Lingam is not just a representation of the physical organ but is a manifestation of the rejuvenating and fertile force of God, often referred to as the "Anandyavana," or the grove of joy. It serves as a reminder of the cosmic cycle of creation, preservation, and destruction. Worshipping the Lingam is believed to confer divine blessings, peace, luck, prosperity, and good fortune.
data.spiritual_symbolism: The term "Lingam" in Hinduism symbolizes the divine phallic symbol representing Shiva, the god of creation. It is believed to be the tangible form of the abstract cosmic energy or consciousness. The Lingam is a reminder of Shiva's creative power and is a focus of worship in temples.
